祥.meaning: On the night the princess is born, a white <part>sheep</part> wanders into the square and curls up under the old <part>lamppost</part>, which flickers on by itself for the first time in years. The village elders nod at each other. Everyone agrees: it's <kanji>auspicious</kanji>.
祥.on: Every year on her birthday, the village puts on a puppet <sound>show</sound> about it.
祥.kun: The sheep gives a happy <sound>sigh</sound>, and the baby answers, '<sound>Wah</sound>!'

遮.meaning: A <part>commoner</part> sits at the foot of the palace <part>ramp</part> with a butterfly net. Every paper plane the princes throw from the balcony, he snatches mid-flight, refolds into a frog and hands back. Not one plane has landed in a year. He loves to <kanji>intercept</kanji>.
遮.on: One day he nets a stray <sound>shu</sound>ttlecock too.
遮.kun: He shares his lunch, a <sound>sa</sound>rdine and an <sound>e</sound>gg, with two passing <sound>gee</sound>se.

癖.meaning: A spice seller runs her <part>chili stall</part> from a <part>leaky shed</part>. Every time a drip lands on her nose she tugs her left ear and winks, and now she does it with no drip at all, even in her sleep. Her customers wink back. It's her famous <kanji>mannerism</kanji>.
癖.on: She lays out her chilies in a neat <sound>hex</sound>agon on the counter.
癖.kun: Even her <sound>cu</sound>ckoo clock seems to wink when it strikes <sound>se</sound>ven.

軌.meaning: Every morning a farmer drives his old <part>car</part> down the same lane to market, and after <part>nine</part> years its wheels have worn two deep grooves in the mud. Now he doesn't even steer. He reads the paper while the car follows the <kanji>rut</kanji>.
軌.on: He just turns the <sound>key</sound> and opens the sports page.

峰.meaning: A lazy climber gets halfway up a <part>mountain</part> and finds a <part>lookout post</part> with a folding chair on top. He climbs the post instead, sits down, and waves at the real climbers struggling above him. From his chair it feels just like the <kanji>summit</kanji>.
峰.on: Someone up top sprays him with a garden <sound>ho</sound>se for cheating.
峰.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat shares his chair and holds his butterfly <sound>ne</sound>t.

訂.meaning: A mayor writes a <part>speech</part> to open a new <part>street</part>. A dog chews page two, so he rewrites it; rain smudges page three, so he rewrites that; a pigeon lands on the rest. He scribbles all night under a lamp. By dawn it's version forty. He just loves to <kanji>revise</kanji>.
訂.on: He sticks each new page over the old one with sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe.
訂.kun: At the opening he cries, '<sound>Ta</sound>-<sound>da</sound>!', and reads out a single word.

凸.meaning: A girl on the beach packs her <part>bucket</part> with wet sand and turns out a wide mound, then plonks a small wooden <part>frame</part> on top as a tower. A crab climbs to the peak and looks down at the bulge. Anything that swells outward like that, her teacher says, is <kanji>convex</kanji>.
凸.on: The crab holds up a <sound>to</sound>rch and sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'
凸.kun: From a <sound>de</sound>ckchair beside it, a <sound>ko</sound>ala pats its own round tummy.
